title: Build aven, our agent harness
note: The first AIP of aven's new sequence: aven is built with its own steps, by hand, before any of it is automated. The 91 current intents (theOS/docs/intents.json, numbered OLD-AIP-1 to OLD-AIP-91) are consolidated into this format later, in their own AIP.

who: Samuel, the one person who decides, whose attention is the scarcest resource.
The agents that do the work, in 20 to 50 parallel threads (CLAUDE.md).
Anyone who later needs to know why something is the way it is.
problem.experience: Samuel catches problems the agents should have caught, and repeats corrections.

items.text: The intent detail page broke: two parts of the page shared one CSS class name.
The scenario table squeezed its first column into a tall strip.
The intents and decisions pages did not scroll.
The board scrolled as a whole instead of per column.
Not every "rule" was renamed to "policy" after that was decided.
Slides kept an old shape of operations after its single source of truth changed.
The published page was not updated after a change.

evidence.group: Judgement, which belongs at Gate A

items.text: Agents were modelled without their own identity, and coops with members.
An audit leaned on summaries instead of primary sources.

problem.baseline: Ten corrections by Samuel in one session (31 Oct to 1 Nov 2026, 67 commits to theOS), outside any gate: 1.5 per 10 commits. Seven were escapes, problems in work already called done (four layout, three sweeps); three were judgement.
whys: Samuel catches problems the agent should have caught. Why? The agent checks its own work, and only what it thinks of.
Why? Nothing independent checks the work against what a person sees, and nothing says beforehand what must be true.
Root cause: nothing independent checks the work against what a person sees, and nothing says beforehand what must be true.
problem.whys_note: The first draft went two whys further (the process lives in chat; there is no record). The zoom-out review showed that none of the ten came from lost context: those two whys described the planned solution, not the cause. They were removed.
truths: A language model is not deterministic; programs and proofs are.

Content that can't be reached is visible to a headless browser; a renamed word with one meaning is visible to a text search; a squeezed column or a stretched chip is visible in a screenshot to a fresh eye.
A checker that shares the author's context tends to agree with it.
A cloud container is reclaimed; only what is committed and pushed survives.
Git keeps every version and who made it.
assumptions: theOS is a standalone, fresh project: everything lives in theOS/, built from scratch. aven touches no code outside theOS/: not maiacity, not avenDB (aven/DB2), not aven/ops, not the repository's .claude or CLAUDE.md. One exception (Samuel, 1 Nov): the sandbox may be used for testing, without changing it.

theOS/ is the single source of truth and our memory: one JSON doc per thing (this intent, its reviews, your decisions, sessions, sources, aven's steps, gates and types). Three viewers show them: Docs, Intents and Sources.

The plan adds, all inside theOS/: theOS/package.json and its lockfile (theOS's own dependencies, such as Playwright), theOS/CLAUDE.md with the done rule, theOS/aven/ (the check command, the crawl, the docs check, the pixel diff, the terms check, the checker's prompt) and theOS/docs/glossary.json.
The 91 current intents and the Intents board are legacy too (Samuel, 1 Nov): learned from; their decisions and lessons move into aven's format in a later consolidation AIP.
Viewer changes (theOS/docs) are ordinary edits under the done rule, not part of this AIP.
Samuel is the only one who passes a gate.
problem.risk: Can be undone: everything is files in git, inside theOS/. Nothing outside: no push to main, no deploy, nothing outside theOS changed.

reuse.use: Used (theOS): the viewer; one file per record, its stage computed from its events.
Legacy (Samuel, 1 Nov): learned from; its decisions and lessons move into aven's format when they are consolidated.

reuse.what: avenSANDBOX (aven/DB2/SANDBOX.md: the box and its browsers)
reuse.use: Used for testing, by Samuel's exception (1 Nov): theOS's checks may run in it; nothing in it is changed.
Learned from, not touched: what a check of a hash-routed docs app checks (every view draws, no sideways scroll, wide tables in their own box, contrast, minimum slide text, a screenshot per view).
Learned from, not touched: the format for decided renames (→ x), words with two meanings (⚠) and their scopes.
Learned from, not touched: its no-page-scroll rule fits /app, not theOS/docs, where a phone page scrolls by design.
Learned from, not touched: pick the checks a change needs from its paths.
Learned from, not touched: an append-only check compares a log with its earlier version.
Learned from, not touched: measure, change one thing, keep or revert, with a verdict.
Learned from, not touched: one claim checked with evidence lines; independent agents trying to refute a divergence.

options.name: Keep as is
options.note: Rejected: ten escapes in one session.

options.name: Checks first
options.note: The done rule for every theOS commit: theOS's check command green (the crawl, a pixel diff against the base commit, the docs check, the terms check), a fresh checker's look at every view whose pixels changed, pushed and published. An AIP only for work that needs Gate A. Everything in theOS/, from scratch. Measure over three sessions; the router, the Stop hook and a metrics script only as new AIPs, and only if escapes remain.

options.name: The full harness now
options.note: Records for every intent, a router, a Stop hook, a metrics script. Rejected for now: it would not have caught any of the ten, and aven automates last.

options.name: Adopt an existing harness whole
options.note: Rejected: none keeps our records, gates or Lean; they stay sources.

claims.promise: The docs check fails at the parent of faf266961, where content could not be reached, and passes now.
claims.fails: It checks something a person does not see, or is tuned to the known bug.
claims.check: Its rule (every scroll container whose content is taller than it can scroll; no view scrolls sideways) is committed before the replay, then run at 390x844, 1280x720 and 1440x900.

claims.promise: The crawl reaches every state a person can reach from theOS/index.html, following every link and button and dropping duplicate states, on any commit.
claims.fails: A state behind a button, or a renamed data file, is never seen.
claims.check: Run on the current commit and on the parents of 106ba0e5f, 3ddc07339 and faf266961: it reaches the intent pages and their Learn tabs with no edit per commit.

claims.promise: A pixel diff against the base commit lists the views that changed, and a fresh checker shown only those flags the broken ones.
claims.fails: A visual break is called done, or the author picks which views are seen.
claims.check: Replayed on the commits that introduced the stretched chip, the squeezed table and the board that scrolled as a whole (found by bisecting with the crawl's screenshots): the checker flags each; its prompt and answer are stored.

claims.promise: The terms check fails when a renamed word comes back where its rename applies, stays quiet where the word keeps its other meaning, and passes now.
claims.fails: A rename sweep misses a place, or a word with two meanings raises a false alarm.
claims.check: A test plants each renamed word once where the rename applies (story ids, slide text fields) and once where its other meaning is correct (for example the rules of an Architecture panel); each entry cites the OLD-AIP that decided it.

outcome.promise: Over the next three sessions of theOS work: zero layout escapes, zero renamed-term escapes, and fewer corrections per 10 commits than this session's 1.5 (10 in 67 commits).
outcome.how: Tallied by hand per session, with the session's commit count; within an AIP each correction is also an event by Samuel (what: correction).

gaps: The operations-shape sweep (one of the three sweeps) has no check; the pixel-diff checker may catch it, nothing promises it.
Running theOS's check command is part of the done rule, not enforced: enforcement is the deferred Stop hook.
done_rule: A change to theOS is done when theOS's check command is green (the crawl, the pixel diff against the base commit, the docs check and the terms check), a fresh checker has looked at every view whose pixels changed and found no Blocker or Major, it is pushed to the work branch, and the theOS docs page (a private artifact) is republished, its version noted in the commit message. In theOS, the repository's root check (aven/ops/devx/check.mjs) does not apply.
aip_when: An AIP is opened for work that needs your Gate A: a decision about what must be true (architecture, product behaviour, how we work). Small edits follow the done rule only.

checkpoints.adds: theOS/CLAUDE.md with the done rule (it says the root check does not apply in theOS); theOS/package.json and its lockfile; the check command; the terms check over theOS/docs/glossary.json, with its test.
The crawl and the docs check: every reachable state from theOS/index.html at 390x844, 1280x720 and 1440x900, the reachability rule, a screenshot of each; their replays; the done rule extended.
The pixel diff against the base commit, the checker's prompt in theOS/aven/checkers/, its replays; the done rule extended.

deferred.until: Three intents were run by hand and escapes remain.
Agents are measured stopping early. Then: only on branches with an open record, honouring stop_hook_active, never blocking on Gate A or B.

deferred.what: Consolidating the 91 current intents into this format
deferred.until: A later AIP (Samuel, 1 Nov: "we consolidate the current AIPs later into the new flow format"). Their decisions have no claims or checkpoints yet, so that AIP decides how each maps.
aven releases anything on its own.
There are three or more records.
Records multiply; git keeps their history meanwhile.

deleted: Anything in legacy code: rules in the repository's check.mjs, entries in aven/ops/ci/suites.json, agents in the repository's .claude, a line in its CLAUDE.md. theOS is standalone (Samuel, 1 Nov).
Choosing which views the checker sees: the pixel diff chooses.
Picking checks by path: there is one app, and every check always runs.
Contrast and slide text size: no escape asked for them.
The memory and decision-history section: it moved into aven's definition.
A separate lessons file: lessons stay in aven's definition.

questions.q: Does your chat message, quoted into the record with its time, count as your approval at a gate?
Round 3 was not clean, the third round in a row. aven's rule stops here and asks you: what next? Since revision 5 you decided D-7 to D-20, which change the design again.
options: Revision 6, then round 4 (recommended): fold in D-7 to D-20, and hand the memory parts (decisions, terms, the trace) to AIP-3, brain, so AIP-1 is only aven's flow, its checkers and the apps
Round 4 on revision 5 as it is
